items.name: Hanging Rock Summit Walk, Hanging Rock Reserve
items.venue: 139 South Rock Rd, Woodend (under an hour from Melbourne)
items.note: A moderate 1.8 km return climb (60–90 min) through boulders to views of Mt Macedon and Camels Hump; go early or late on warm days, when grey kangaroos graze nearby.

items.name: Organ Pipes walk and picnic, Organ Pipes National Park
items.venue: Organ Pipes NP, near Keilor North
items.note: Basalt columns, Rosette Rock and the Tessellated Pavement about 1.5 hrs on foot, a short drive from the city; Parks Vic suggests morning to mid-afternoon in summer, and spring can bring kangaroo and wallaby joeys. Steep path.

items.name: Steavenson Falls Walk, Marysville
items.when: Any day; falls floodlit dusk to midnight
items.venue: Falls Rd, Marysville (about 2 hrs from Melbourne)
items.note: Short all-abilities walk to the base of one of Victoria's tallest waterfalls (84 m), with stone steps up to a top lookout; a warm-evening visit to see the falls floodlit is the twist.

items.name: Cape Schanck Lighthouse Reserve boardwalk
items.note: Short circuit, then the staircase and boardwalk down to the rock platform with lookouts over Pulpit Rock and Devils Desk; good for sunsets and coastal wildflowers. Watch for big waves on the rocks.

items.name: You Yangs mountain bike trails (Kurrajong Plantation & Stockyards)
items.venue: You Yangs Regional Park, Little River
items.note: Over 50 km of signed trails: Kurrajong's 20 km of flatter loops suit families, while Stockyards has rocky singletrack and three downhill runs.

items.name: Federation Trail, Brooklyn to Werribee
items.note: A 23 km off-road path along the old outfall sewer, flat and easy, with the Brooklyn section freshly resurfaced; pair it with lunch in Werribee.

items.name: Great Southern Rail Trail
items.venue: Nyora to Yarram, South Gippsland (about 130 km SE of Melbourne)
items.note: 136 km of crushed granite and fine gravel through rolling South Gippsland dairy country; ride a section as a day trip or do it over a weekend.

items.name: Murray to Mountains Rail Trail
items.venue: Wangaratta to Bright, plus Yackandandah and Rutherglen branches
items.note: 137 km of sealed trail into the High Country; an early-summer weekend away with wineries and Bright at the end.

items.name: Guns N' Roses: World Tour 2026, with Airbourne
items.note: Classic hard-rock legends in stadium mode, with Aussie rockers Airbourne opening; tickets still on general sale.

items.name: Kool & The Gang and Sister Sledge ft. Sledgendary
items.note: A double bill of funk and disco hits, from Celebration to We Are Family.

items.name: Kim Wilde: Closer Tour
items.note: This Saturday: the 80s pop star of Kids In America and You Keep Me Hangin' On.

items.name: Mark Seymour Orchestrated
items.note: The Hunters & Collectors frontman with his band and a full orchestra, marking 40 years of songs.

items.name: Dermot Kennedy: The Weight of the Woods Tour
items.note: This Saturday: the big-voiced Irish singer-songwriter in arena mode.

items.name: Stewart Copeland: Police Deranged for Orchestra
items.note: The Police's drummer plays Roxanne, Every Breath You Take and more with a 28-piece orchestra, his first Australian shows since the 2007–08 reunion tour. A natural one after Sting.

items.name: Train: Drops of Jupiter 25th anniversary tour, with Barenaked Ladies
items.note: General sale from today (Thu 19 Nov, 9am); Barenaked Ladies' first Australian tour in over 25 years.

items.name: Belinda Carlisle: G'Day & Goodbye
items.note: Billed as her farewell to Australian audiences, spanning her solo hits back to The Go-Go's.

items.name: Diana Krall
items.note: Just announced: presale Mon 23 Nov 11am, general sale Wed 25 Nov 10am. A jazz-pop great in a theatre-sized room.

items.name: Bachman-Turner Overdrive: No Speed Limit Tour
items.note: The Canadian classic-rock band's first-ever Australian tour, with Randy Bachman's catalogue going back to The Guess Who.

items.name: The Human League: Generations – Greatest Hits Tour
items.note: A second Melbourne show has been added for the 80s synth-pop hitmakers.

items.name: David Cross: Fake Joy
items.note: His first-ever Australian tour, from Mr. Show and Arrested Development's Tobias. Tickets on sale tomorrow, Fri 20 Nov, 10am.

items.name: Jim Jefferies: Son of a Carpenter – Resurrected
items.note: One night only from the US-based Aussie whose edgy style sits close to Carr and CK; on sale now.

items.name: Zarna Garg: The Million Dollar Tour
items.note: The Indian-American comic and immigrant mum with Amazon and Hulu specials and more than a billion social views.

items.name: Arj Barker: The Eleventh Hour
items.note: The American comic's 11th national tour, with a long comedy-festival season.

items.name: Australia v England Men's T20I
items.note: News: it's this Saturday night, a summer-opening Ashes-flavoured T20 under lights.

items.name: WBBL|12 Melbourne Derby: Stars v Renegades
items.note: Women's Big Bash cross-town derby this Sunday at the intimate Junction Oval.

items.name: Sheffield Shield: Victoria v Queensland
items.note: A cheap, uncrowded day of first-class cricket in the Members' Reserve, three weeks before the Boxing Day Test.

items.name: BBL|16: Melbourne Renegades v Hobart Hurricanes (Christmas Eve)
items.note: The first Big Bash game ever played on Christmas Eve, a prime-time match under Junction Oval's new lights.

items.name: Melbourne United v NZ Breakers (Indigenous Round)
items.note: This Saturday. News: United beat the Phoenix 102–95 in Throwdown 35 last weekend.

items.name: SE Melbourne Phoenix v Cairns Taipans
items.note: This Sunday afternoon, a kid-friendly time slot; the Phoenix's last Melbourne-arena game until 19 Dec.

items.name: Melbourne United v Brisbane Bullets
items.note: Sunday-afternoon game; United beat Brisbane 120–92 at home on 7 Nov.

items.name: Melbourne United v Tasmania JackJumpers
items.note: Saturday-night game before United's road trips to Perth and Illawarra.

items.name: SE Melbourne Phoenix v Perth Wildcats (regional home game)
items.venue: Gippsland Regional Indoor Sports Stadium, Traralgon
items.note: A rare Phoenix home game in Gippsland; worth it if you're heading that way.

items.name: SE Melbourne Phoenix v Sydney Kings / Melbourne United v Cairns Taipans
items.note: Two pre-Christmas home games to round out the window.

items.name: Stereophonic (MTC)
items.note: Broadway's most Tony-nominated play ever (five wins), about a 70s rock band recording a legendary album, with music by ex-Arcade Fire member Will Butler. Book now.

items.name: Mrs. Doubtfire: The Musical
items.note: News: the Australian premiere opens next Wednesday, with Melbourne seeing it before Sydney.

items.name: The Nutcracker (BIG Live)
items.note: Tchaikovsky's Christmas ballet returns after a sell-out 2025 season, with a longer run this year; 2 hrs including interval.

items.name: The Christmas Spectacular: A Magical Wonderland
items.note: A family festive show of singers, dancers, circus acts and illusions.

items.name: Lifelike: Puppets, Movies & Magic
items.note: News: opens tomorrow. A world premiere on screen puppetry, from Jurassic Park and Labyrinth to The Muppets and Agro.

items.name: Barbie: The Exhibition
items.note: News: opens next Saturday. Over 250 dolls from London's Design Museum, including the 1959 'Number 1 Barbie' and the 1962 Dreamhouse.

items.name: Love Letters
items.venue: Heide Museum of Modern Art, Bulleen
items.note: Global contemporary artists on longing and attachment, as artworks in the form of heartfelt letters; pair it with Heide's gardens.

items.name: Bondi: A Curated Tour of Remembrance
items.venue: Jewish Museum of Australia, St Kilda
items.note: Ticketed. One year on from the Bondi attack, a curated tour linking Chanukah, Jewish life in Australia and Bondi, including a surf club rescue board used that day.

items.name: Alliance Française Christmas Market
items.note: This weekend: French food, artisan gifts, live music and free beginner French taster classes.

items.name: The Oddities & Curiosities Expo
items.note: This weekend: the world's largest touring oddities market, with taxidermy, antiques, curios and sideshow performers.

items.name: QVM Christmas Night Market
items.note: News: the first night is next Wednesday. European-style festive food and gifts, fully undercover.

items.name: Christmas Makers Market at Como House
items.note: Handmade art, design and food stalls on a historic estate's lawns.

items.name: Trust Makers' Market at Rippon Lea
items.note: The last makers' market of the year on the estate's lawns, handy for last-minute gifts close to Bentleigh.
